caption:
A brief that only works in a command post is not enough. It has to hold up in a courtroom, a board of inquiry, an after-action review.

That means every finding is labeled confirmed, assessed, or unknown — and stays labeled that way through the chain. No upgrading an assessment to a fact because the reader wants certainty. No dropping a caveat because it complicates the story.

The method is slower than a confident guess. It is also the only version that survives someone asking, later, how you knew.

card.headline: Built to survive the question later
card.sub: Every finding is labeled confirmed, assessed, or unknown — and the label doesn't change to fit the room.

rationale: Establishes the mission's evidentiary-accountability angle without repeating prior confirmed/assessed/unknown posts, framing it around judicial durability rather than operational tuning.
